key_insight: Forcing-informed resolvent analysis uses data-derived forcing and response subspaces to recover physically consistent input-output modes and gains in self-sustained unsteady flows.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable reduced-order models and flow control diagnostics for wakes and transitional flows, especially where nonlinear forcing dominates.
method: Estimate input and output subspaces from simulation snapshots of forcing and response.
Build a forcing-informed resolvent operator using these bases and extract mode pairs and singular values.
Optionally infer the linear operator directly from forcing snapshots for a fully data-driven analysis.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated on the Stuart-Landau oscillator and demonstrated on a 2D cylinder wake and 3D transitional boundary layer, successfully identifying gains and mode pairs at nonlinear frequencies.
watch_item: The approach depends on quality simulation data and subspace estimation, so noisy or insufficient snapshots may limit mode recovery and interpretation.
paper_title: Forcing-informed resolvent analysis: Identification of input-output relations in self-sustained flows
